rationale: The model's own shipped objective; same reaction used for S85 in the 002 cross-scale benchmark, included so the sweep average can be compared back to that ~10x result directly.
Liver is the model's largest, most metabolically central organ compartment (highest reaction count of any organ).
Kidney is the second-largest organ compartment and central to whole-body nitrogen/electrolyte handling.
Brain has distinct, highly constrained energy metabolism (near-exclusive glucose/ketone use) vs. other organs.
Heart is a large, continuously-active muscle compartment with fatty-acid-dominant metabolism.
Skeletal muscle is the largest body-mass compartment overall, dominant in whole-body amino-acid/glucose turnover.
Colon sits directly at the host-microbiome interface, coupling host metabolism to gut microbial exchange.
Pancreas governs whole-body glucose homeostasis (insulin/glucagon producing tissue).
Lung is a large, distinct gas-exchange compartment with its own surfactant/lipid metabolism.
Skin is a large peripheral compartment, structurally and metabolically distinct from internal organs.
Adipose tissue is the body's primary lipid-storage compartment, metabolically distinct from lean organs.
B cells represent adaptive humoral immunity, a small peripheral compartment contrasting with the large organ objectives.
CD4+ T cells represent adaptive cell-mediated immunity.
NK cells represent innate lymphoid immunity, distinct lineage from the adaptive T/B-cell objectives.
Monocytes represent innate myeloid immunity and phagocytic metabolism, distinct from lymphoid cell types.
Platelets are anucleate blood cells with minimal biosynthetic machinery -- the smallest, most constrained objective in the set.
Common gut commensal/opportunistic pathogen; representative Bacteroidetes-phylum taxon.
Major butyrate-producing commensal, widely used as a marker of gut health in microbiome studies.
Facultative anaerobe and common gut pathobiont; representative Proteobacteria-phylum taxon.
Mucin-degrading commensal associated with host metabolic health; representative Verrucomicrobia-phylum taxon.
